Lemma
[Ricci controls the harmonic $C^{1,\alpha }$ norm]

Source: petersen:page-0439, petersen:page-0440 ↗ def:pet-ch11-harmonic-norm ↗ lem:pet-ch11-laplacian-ricci-harmonic-coords ↗ thm:pet-ch11-schauder-estimates 1. ch11:11.4.1If $|\Ric |\le \Lambda $ and $r_1<r_2$, $K\ge \| (M,g,p)\| ^{\mathrm{har}}_{C^{1,r_2}}$, $\alpha \in (0,1)$ there is $C(n,\alpha ,K,r_1,r_2,\Lambda )$ with $\| (M,g,p)\| ^{\mathrm{har}}_{C^{1,\alpha },r_1}\le C$. If moreover $g$ is Einstein, $\Ric =kg$, then for each $m$ there is $C(n,\alpha ,K,r_1,r_2,k,m)$ with $\| (M,g,p)\| ^{\mathrm{har}}_{C^{m+1,\alpha },r_1}\le C$.
Proof

↗ lem:pet-ch11-anderson-ricci-harmonic-c1alpha-bound \sketch In a controlled harmonic chart, apply subsection 2.2 to the metric equation from subsection 2.3,

\[ \Delta g_{ij}=-2\Ric _{ij}-2Q(g,\partial g). \]

The $C^1$ chart bound controls ellipticity and the quadratic term, while $|\Ric |\le \Lambda $ controls the remainder, giving the $C^{1,\alpha }$ estimate on the smaller ball. If $\Ric =kg$, the right side gains the regularity of $g$; iterated Schauder estimates yield every $C^{m+1,\alpha }$ bound.

□
